relevance_reason: The paper reports a consanguineous family with a homozygous-presumed ABCA2 frameshift variant causing ataxia with dysarthria. It widens the phenotype of the ABCA2-related disorder this entry covers.

findings.statement: Aslam and Naz (2019) reported 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family who had cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria. Brain MRI of the older sib was normal. Both affected individuals had elevated levels of low density lipoproteins in the blood.
quotes: The study was conducted to identify the molecular basis of a movement disorder in a consanguineous Pakistani family.
Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria. Magnetic resonance imaging did not reveal brain abnormalities.
The levels of low density lipid proteins were elevated in blood samples of both affected individuals.

findings.statement: Aslam and Naz (2019) used whole-exome sequencing in 2 sibs with ataxia and dysarthria from a consanguineous Pakistani family and identified a frameshift variant in the ABCA2 gene, c.4993delG (p.Val1665TyrfsTer36; NM_212533.2). Sanger sequencing showed that the variant segregated with the disorder. It was absent from all publicly available databases and from ethnically matched controls.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing data analyses identified a frameshift variant, c.4993delG:p.(Val1665TyrfsTer36) in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2) which segregated with the disorder and was absent from all publicly available databases and ethnically matched controls.

findings.statement: Aslam and Naz (2019) noted that recessive ABCA2 variants had previously been reported in patients with intellectual disability and global developmental delay. They concluded that their family showed a distinct ataxia-with-dysarthria phenotype, reflecting pleiotropic effects of ABCA2 mutation. They also stated that the phenotype closely matched that of Abca2 knockout mice.
quotes: Although recessively inherited ABCA2 variants have been reported in two patients who had intellectual disability with global developmental delays, our study demonstrates the role of an ABCA2 variant in the pathogenesis of ataxia with dysarthria.
The phenotype observed in our patients shows high concordance with that observed in Abca2 knockout mice.
Our research links an ABCA2 variant with a distinct form of ataxia with dysarthria in humans and demonstrates pleiotropic effects due to the gene mutation.

relevance_reason: Reports two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability in which homozygous truncating ABCA2 variants segregated with the disease. The authors suggested this is a disorder distinct from ABCA2-associated amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

findings.statement: Maddirevula et al. (2019) described 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability. Both families carried homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2, found through autozygome and exome analysis. The index patient (16DG0071) did not have obvious gross dysmorphism. The authors suggested that this phenotype is a distinct allelic disorder, different from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis previously reported with ABCA2.
quotes: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
which is distinct from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis reported by Steinberg et al.
h Facial pictures of index (16DG0071) subject with ABCA2 showing apparent lack of gross dysmorphism.

findings.statement: In one of 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability, Maddirevula et al. (2019) used autozygome and exome analysis to identify a homozygous frameshift variant in ABCA2, c.740dupT (p.Gly248Argfs*38; NM_212533.2). The variant fully segregated with the phenotype in the family.
quotes: homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38]) and (NM_212533.2:c.1027C>T:p.[Gln343*])

findings.statement: In the second family with global developmental delay and intellectual disability, Maddirevula et al. (2019) identified a homozygous nonsense variant in ABCA2, c.1027C>T (p.Gln343*; NM_212533.2). The variant fully segregated with the phenotype in the family.
quotes: homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38]) and (NM_212533.2:c.1027C>T:p.[Gln343*])

relevance_reason: Only the abstract is available. It describes a large exome/genome sequencing study of consanguineous families with intellectual disability but does not name the gene, variant or family relevant to IDPOGSA, so it provides context only.

findings.statement: Hu et al. (2019) performed whole exome and whole genome sequencing in 404 consanguineous, mostly Iranian families with 2 or more affected offspring with intellectual disability. They found likely causative variants in 219 families, involving 77 known and 77 novel autosomal recessive ID (candidate) genes, 21 X-linked genes, and 9 genes previously implicated in diseases other than ID.
quotes: we report on whole exome and whole genome sequencing in 404 consanguineous predominantly Iranian families with two or more affected offspring
In 219 of these, we found likely causative variants, involving 77 known and 77 novel AR-ID (candidate) genes, 21 X-linked genes, as well as 9 genes previously implicated in diseases other than ID.
